_about: Hero vehicle parameters. hue_ranges are HSV [lo,hi] pairs of the PAINT; attach_dark_max_v/_s attach the car's dark part to it (0 = the paint covers the whole car, which is the case for a car painted at both ends). open_kernel removes specks; close_kernel joins the body's halves; min_area rejects smaller things. Re-record the front/rear template afterwards and CHECK corr(right,left) is negative.
_measured: 2026-10-17, yellow nose + black cabin. Paint: H 24..33, S 93..138, V 115..211, stable at 460..500 px every frame. PROBLEM: attaching the black cabin is NOT reliable - the cabin is only ~36 grey levels darker than the road beside it (147 vs 183) while the road itself varies more than that across the frame, so a threshold that catches the cabin on one frame misses it on the next. Measured over 14 frames: the mask flipped between the whole car (3,175 px, axis 0 deg) and the nose alone (460 px) six times, and the reported position moved +/-17 px with it. attach_dark_margin_v is therefore 0: a stable nose with no heading beats a flickering whole car. To get the heading back, either give the car paint at BOTH ends (the previous car was red at both ends, which is exactly why a colour mask covered it), or take the cabin from edges rather than brightness.
